overall_reason: The page is carried by the real product: a working-looking issue view with specific content (DRV-8852 'Faster app launch', 'Render UI before vehicle_state sync', the Slack thread that becomes issues, a triage board), in a consistent, deliberate dark brand; the generic lines are confined to a few headings.

findings.where: hero sub-line, logo strip caption, statement h2, closing CTA
findings.evidence: Fresh-reader lines that fit any AI-era SaaS: 'Purpose-built for planning and building products. Designed for the AI era.', 'POWERING THE COMPANIES BUILDING THE FUTURE', 'Purpose-built for modern teams with AI workflows at its core, Linear sets a new standard for planning and building products.', 'Built for the future. Available today.'
findings.after: Close on something only Linear can say, in the register of the mock: what a team stops doing once issues come from Slack threads and agents open the PRs.
findings.why: Rival-name swap: these four lines stay true for any product-tool competitor; they are the weakest text on an otherwise specific page.

findings.evidence: Seven-logo strip (OpenAI, Vercel, Salesforce, Figma, Cursor, Coinbase, Ramp) with a mono caps caption, then a large two-tone statement paragraph; the closing is a centred CTA band and a six-column link footer.
findings.before: Logo strip > statement > ... > CTA band > link footer
findings.after: Keep the logos (they are real customers) but drop the mono caps caption; let the logos link to their case studies.
findings.why: Only 3 stock sections (logo strip, CTA band, link footer) around product-led sections; below the 5 threshold, recorded as polish.

strengths: The hero mock is real product content with a story: Slack report > issue DRV-8852 > agent ('Opus 5.5') opens a draft PR 'Reset dimmed ride rows' with '+22 -10'. Every line fails the rival-name swap in the right way.
The Slack thread (lena, didier, andreas) leading to '@Linear create issues and assign to me' shows intake instead of claiming it.
Consistent, deliberate visual system (dark ground, restrained grey scale, one type family, two-tone headings used as a house style, not borrowed).
not_investigated: disputed: sweep SLP-012 violet-gradient (#6d78d5, gradient pair) comes from product-mock accents such as the Slack send button and status colours, not from a page look; INT-005 'Todo' residue is a real workflow state in the board mock.
Several sections render partly dark/empty in the 1440 tiles (agent windows); 14 script chunks were blocked (manifest network), so some animation states are missing.
